memorymarshal-cast.title: Reinterpret span element types with MemoryMarshal.Cast
memorymarshal-cast.short: View the same memory as another unmanaged element type
memorymarshal-cast.summary: MemoryMarshal.Cast exposes the bytes behind a Span or ReadOnlySpan as elements of another non-reference type without copying them.
memorymarshal-cast.why: Binary processing can work with structured values in an existing buffer without allocating a temporary array.
memorymarshal-cast.tips: The element types cannot contain references. When reading external formats, also account for endianness and layout.

sequencereader-delimited.title: Read delimited data across buffers with SequenceReader
sequencereader-delimited.short: Parse a ReadOnlySequence without joining its segments
sequencereader-delimited.summary: SequenceReader<T> advances through a ReadOnlySequence<T>, including values that span multiple segments.
sequencereader-delimited.why: Data from PipeReader and similar sources can be searched for delimiters or fixed values without copying segments into one array.
sequencereader-delimited.tips: When the complete value has not arrived yet, preserve the appropriate consumed position and wait for more input instead of treating partial data as complete.

dateonly-daynumber.title: Compute days between dates with DateOnly.DayNumber
dateonly-daynumber.short: Do date arithmetic without adding a time or time zone
dateonly-daynumber.summary: DateOnly represents a calendar date, and DayNumber exposes that date as a consecutive integer suitable for simple day differences.
dateonly-daynumber.why: Birthdays, due dates, and other date-only values do not need a midnight DateTime as a stand-in.
dateonly-daynumber.tips: Use DateTimeOffset or another instant-aware type when time and time-zone meaning matters; keep DateOnly for genuinely date-only data.

timeonly-between.title: Represent and subtract times with TimeOnly
timeonly-between.short: Work with times of day that have no date
timeonly-between.summary: TimeOnly represents a time within a day, and subtracting two TimeOnly values produces a TimeSpan.
timeonly-between.why: Opening hours and recurring daily schedules can be modeled without attaching an arbitrary date.
timeonly-between.tips: For intervals that cross a date boundary, simple subtraction may not represent the intended elapsed duration; include the date when it matters.

uri-trycreate.title: Parse URIs safely with Uri.TryCreate
uri-trycreate.short: Validate URI syntax without using exceptions for normal failures
uri-trycreate.summary: Uri.TryCreate parses text using a requested UriKind and returns a Uri only when parsing succeeds.
uri-trycreate.why: User input and other expected-to-fail values can be checked without exception-driven control flow.
uri-trycreate.tips: Successful parsing is not a security decision. Validate Scheme, Host, and other components against the requirements of the operation.

httpclient-json.title: Read JSON responses directly with HttpClient JSON extensions
httpclient-json.short: Combine GET and deserialization with GetFromJsonAsync
httpclient-json.summary: System.Net.Http.Json GetFromJsonAsync combines an HTTP GET with System.Text.Json deserialization.
httpclient-json.why: Common JSON API calls need less boilerplate than reading the response as a string and then deserializing it separately.
httpclient-json.tips: Pass a CancellationToken. Use HttpResponseMessage directly when you need custom status handling, headers, or other response details.

json-naming-policy.title: Set JSON property naming with JsonNamingPolicy
json-naming-policy.short: Apply conventions such as snake_case consistently
json-naming-policy.summary: JsonSerializerOptions.PropertyNamingPolicy controls how model property names are converted to JSON property names.
json-naming-policy.why: A shared API naming convention can be applied centrally instead of adding an attribute to every property.
json-naming-policy.tips: Choose a policy that matches the existing wire format and test compatibility in both serialization and deserialization.

filesystemwatcher-events.title: Receive file change notifications with FileSystemWatcher
filesystemwatcher-events.summary: FileSystemWatcher raises events for file creation, changes, deletion, renaming, and related directory activity.
filesystemwatcher-events.why: Applications can react to configuration or inbox-directory changes without repeatedly scanning the whole directory.
filesystemwatcher-events.tips: Notifications can be duplicated and bursts can overflow the internal buffer. Do not assume one event always corresponds to exactly one logical change.

process-waitforexitasync.title: Await process termination with Process.WaitForExitAsync
process-waitforexitasync.short: Wait for an external process without blocking a thread
process-waitforexitasync.summary: WaitForExitAsync asynchronously waits for a Process to exit and accepts a CancellationToken for canceling the wait.
process-waitforexitasync.why: GUI and server code can avoid occupying a thread with synchronous WaitForExit while an external process runs.
process-waitforexitasync.tips: Canceling the wait does not terminate the external process. Define process termination separately when your application requires it.

regex-nonbacktracking.title: Avoid regex backtracking with RegexOptions.NonBacktracking
regex-nonbacktracking.short: Use predictable matching for supported patterns
regex-nonbacktracking.summary: RegexOptions.NonBacktracking selects the non-backtracking regular-expression engine.
regex-nonbacktracking.why: For supported patterns it avoids input-dependent backtracking explosions and makes matching time easier to bound.
regex-nonbacktracking.tips: The engine does not support every regex feature. Verify that your pattern is compatible and consider a timeout where appropriate.
